patients.label: 62-year-old man undergoing cerebral aneurysm clipping who developed ventricular tachycardia after mannitol
attribution_limitations: The source states it is not clear why VT occurred; transient potassium elevation from myocardial ischemia, mannitol and craniotomy are offered only as possible contributors. No cause of the VT is asserted.

Preoperative is placed before 12-lead ECG and routine laboratory tests; the sodium and potassium values are treated as preoperative on that coordinated phrase. The source also gives a preoperative renal function statement in the discussion.
The blood pressure value below 40 mmHg is not labelled systolic or mean and its sentence has no time of its own; it follows the statement that VT occurred.

The arterial blood gas values and potassium 6.4 mEq/L are in one results sentence with no time of its own; the abstract places the potassium after recovery from VT. The 60 min and 2 min intervals do not name what they are counted from.

The chest compression sentence states no indication of its own; it follows the statements that VT occurred and that blood pressure decreased to below 40 mmHg, and no indication is recorded on the procedure.
Telmisartan and sodium valproate are listed together for hypertension and symptomatic epilepsy; which drug treated which condition is not stated.
Discussion and background statements about mannitol-induced hyperkalemia, published cases and ECG findings in hyperkalemia are general or literature statements, not facts about this patient.

claims.text: A 62-year-old man (173 cm, 64 kg) was scheduled for clipping of an unruptured anterior communicating cerebral artery aneurysm via craniotomy. He had previously received telmisartan and sodium valproate for hypertension and symptomatic epilepsy after a cranial hematoma from right occipital lobe bleeding. Preoperative 12-lead ECG and laboratory tests included serum sodium 141 mEq/L and potassium 4.1 mEq/L. On arrival in the operating room his hemodynamic state was stable.
